newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close higher but shy of record.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close higher but shy of record.

text.p: French shares staged a strong rally on Tuesday, helped by the dollar and bullish underlying sentiment, and closed a whisper away from their all-time high reached on February 18 of this year.

Toward the close the market closely followed the small swings of the Dow Jones Index with Wall Street investors on their toes as Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan adressed the house of representatives.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended up 51.43 points or 1.98 percent at 2,651.69 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,661 from 2,606 on Monday's close.
The all-time high for the CAC-40 index stands at 2,658.62 and Tuesday's trading high was 2,653.65.
* Volume was 8.38 billion francs of which 6.84 billion in blue-chip shares.
* Main pending events are the German unemployment figures on Thursday, which could show an increase, and the U.S. jobs data on Friday which could reveal a decline, economists said.

* Dassault Electronique was the biggest riser with an 8.61 percent gain at 719 francs after a newspaper report 58 percent owner Dassault Industrie could transfer the unit to Thomson-CSF as part of a complex privatisation deal.
* The Le Monde newspaper said that the state could publish a key document about the pending private placement of its 58 percent stake in defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF as soon as Friday.
* Alcatel, up 3.58 percent at 608 francs, had no comment on a report in La Tribune which said it detailed the group's project to acquire the stake in conjunction with Aerospatiale and Dassault.
* Biggest fallers were Sidel, down 3.53 percent to 410.50 francs after Gaz et Eaux reduced its stake, and tobacco group Seita on a cigarette price news report.
* Biggest volume was in Usinor Sacilor, with 1.5 million shares, which rose with a metal share sector supported by the dollar and base metal prices.
* Aluminium group Pechiney, set to report a big 1996 loss after charges on Thursday, gained 5.37 percent at 255 francs.

* Renault closed 1.36 percent up at 141.90 francs, recovering earlier losses today as some investors took profits after a big rise on the back of a Belgian plant closure plan and French job cuts. Industry Minister Franck Borotra urged talks about the financing of the job cut plan.
* Danone, up 3.98 percent at 915 francs, was supported by Morgan Stanley putting it on its list of recommended European stocks, instead of Generale des Eaux .
* Sportswear group Salomon SA. closed 3.21 percent higher at 421 francs after a 7.38 percent opening gain.
The company is resuming its upward trend after some profit-taking in February which dented a long and steady climb.
